conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Preferential Discharge Theory & Aqueous NaCl Electrolysis
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Preferential Discharge Theory & Aqueous NaCl Electrolysis

summaryBox.title: Preferential Discharge
summaryBox.takeaway: Cathode: Ion with HIGHER reduction potential discharges first. Anode: Ion with LOWER reduction potential discharges first. Overpotential can alter kinetic order (e.g. Cl₂ vs O₂).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ELECTROLYSIS OF AQUEOUS NaCl (BRINE)

• Anode Reaction:   2Cl⁻(aq) ──► Cl₂(g) + 2e⁻  (Overpotential suppresses O₂ evolution)
• Cathode Reaction: 2H₂O(l) + 2e⁻ ──► H₂(g) + 2OH⁻(aq)  (E° = -0.83 V > -2.71 V for Na⁺)
• Residual Solution: Accumulates Na⁺ and OH⁻ ions ⟹ pH RISES!
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Cathode (Reduction)**: Between $\text{Na}^+$ ($E^\circ = -2.71\text{ V}$) and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($E^\circ = -0.83\text{ V}$), water is reduced preferentially, liberating $\mathbf{\text{H}_2(g)}$.
• **Anode (Oxidation)**: Thermodynamically $\text{O}_2$ evolution is favored, but due to **Oxygen Overpotential**, oxidation of $\text{Cl}^-$ is kinetically faster, releasing $\mathbf{\text{Cl}_2(g)}$.
• **Solution**: Accumulates $\text{OH}^-$ ions, causing $\mathbf{\text{pH to rise}}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Faraday's Quantitative Laws of Electrolysis
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Faraday's Quantitative Laws of Electrolysis
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FARADAY'S QUANTITATIVE LAWS

1. Faraday's First Law: w = Z × I × t = (M × I × t) / (n × 96485)
   where Z = Equivalent Mass / 96485 = M / (n × 96485)

2. Faraday's Second Law: w₁ / w₂ = E₁ / E₂ = Z₁ / Z₂ (for series connections)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **First Law**: Mass deposited is directly proportional to charge ($q = I \cdot t$): $\mathbf{w = \frac{M \cdot I \cdot t}{n \cdot 96485}}$.
• **Second Law**: When the same charge passes through different electrolytic cells in series, $\mathbf{\frac{w_1}{w_2} = \frac{E_1}{E_2}}$.

quickRevision: Aqueous NaCl electrolysis: Anode = Cl₂, Cathode = H₂, Solution = NaOH (pH rises).
w₁ / w₂ = E₁ / E₂ in series.
